question: In addition to the vessel operator's own 30-day reporting deadline, how quickly must a marine safety enforcement officer who investigates a reportable boating incident file a written report with TPWD?
choice_a: Not later than the 15th day after the officer initially became aware of the incident
choice_d: There is no deadline for the investigating officer to file a report
explanation: Parks and Wildlife Code Section 31.105(c) requires a marine safety enforcement officer who investigates a reportable boating incident in the regular course of duty to electronically file a written report with TPWD no later than the 15th day after first becoming aware of the incident -- a separate, shorter deadline than the operator's own 30-day duty under 31.105(b).
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.105(c) -- officer reporting deadline

question: If an authorized federal official or agency, such as the U.S. Coast Guard, requests information about a Texas boating incident, what is TPWD's obligation under Section 31.105?
choice_a: TPWD is prohibited from ever sharing incident information with any federal agency
choice_b: TPWD must send the requesting federal official or agency any information available to it under the incident reporting requirement
choice_c: TPWD may only share information with the vessel owner's own insurance company
choice_d: TPWD must destroy the report rather than release it to a federal agency
explanation: Section 31.105(d) requires TPWD, on request from an authorized official or agency of the United States, to send that entity any incident information available to the department under the section.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.105(d) -- release of incident information to federal officials

question: What must a Texas peace officer or game warden do before being authorized to enforce the Water Safety Act (Parks and Wildlife Code Chapter 31) by arresting people for violations of it?
choice_a: Nothing extra is required beyond a standard peace officer commission
choice_b: Pass the same boater education course required of recreational boaters
choice_c: Be certified by TPWD as a marine safety enforcement officer, under training and certification standards the commission establishes by rule
choice_d: Obtain a captain's license issued by the U.S. Coast Guard
explanation: Section 31.121(a-1) requires all peace officers and game wardens to be certified by TPWD as marine safety enforcement officers to enforce Chapter 31, and the commission sets the training and certification standards by rule.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.121(a-1), (b) -- marine safety enforcement officer certification

question: Which officers does Texas law designate as the primary enforcement officers responsible for enforcing water safety under Parks and Wildlife Code Chapter 31?
choice_d: Game wardens commissioned by the Parks and Wildlife Commission
explanation: Section 31.121(a-2) designates game wardens commissioned by the commission as the primary enforcement officers responsible for enforcing the water-safety provisions of Chapter 31, though other certified peace officers may also enforce it.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.121(a-2) -- game wardens as primary water safety enforcement officers

question: Under Section 31.121, who may assist game wardens in the search for and rescue of victims of water-oriented accidents?
choice_c: No one may assist a game warden with a water search and rescue
choice_d: Only game wardens from other states
explanation: Section 31.121(e) allows state military forces to assist game wardens in searching for and rescuing victims of water-oriented accidents.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.121(e) -- state military forces assisting in search and rescue

question: What must the operator of a vessel underway do upon sighting a rotating or flashing blue beacon light from a water safety vessel?
choice_a: Speed up to try to reach shore before the officer can intervene
choice_b: Immediately reduce power, bring the vessel to no-wake speed, and then stop until the water safety vessel's intention is understood
choice_c: Turn off all lights and continue at the same speed
choice_d: Nothing; a blue beacon light has no legal significance for a civilian boater
explanation: Section 31.123 requires the operator of a vessel underway, on sighting a rotating or flashing blue beacon light, to reduce power immediately, bring the vessel to no-wake speed, and then come to a stop until the water safety vessel's intention is understood.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.123 -- required response to police water safety vessel

question: Before boarding a vessel to conduct a compliance inspection, what must an enforcement officer do?
choice_a: Obtain a signed search warrant from a magistrate
choice_b: Wait for the vessel operator's attorney to be present
choice_c: First identify himself by presenting proper credentials
explanation: Section 31.124(b) requires an officer boarding a vessel to first identify himself by presenting proper credentials.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.124(b) -- officer identification before boarding

question: If an officer conducting a vessel inspection asks to see the vessel's certificate of number, what is the operator's obligation?
choice_a: There is no obligation to show any document to an enforcement officer
choice_b: The operator may refuse unless the officer first produces a warrant
choice_c: The certificate only needs to be shown if the officer requests it in writing 24 hours in advance
choice_d: Show the certificate to the officer on demand; failing to do so is itself a violation of the Water Safety Act
explanation: Section 31.124(c) requires the operator of a vessel required to carry a certificate of number to show it to the officer on demand; failing to do so constitutes a violation of the chapter.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.124(c) -- certificate of number must be shown on demand

question: Under Section 31.124, what happens if a boat operator refuses to obey the directions of an enforcement officer who is acting under the Water Safety Act?
choice_a: It is not permitted; no person operating a boat may refuse to obey such directions
choice_b: The operator may refuse as long as no accident has occurred
choice_c: Refusal is allowed if the operator disagrees with the officer's reasoning
choice_d: Refusal is only prohibited for vessels longer than 26 feet
explanation: Section 31.124(d) prohibits any person operating a boat on the water of the state from refusing to obey the directions of an enforcement officer acting under the chapter.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.124(d) -- duty to obey enforcement officer's directions

question: According to Section 31.124(e), what must always be an arresting officer's paramount consideration during a vessel stop or boarding?
choice_a: Completing the inspection as quickly as possible regardless of conditions
choice_d: Photographing the vessel for department records
explanation: Section 31.124(e) states that the safety of the vessel shall always be the paramount consideration of an arresting officer.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.124(e) -- vessel safety as paramount consideration

question: If an enforcement officer determines during an inspection that a vessel is being used in violation of the Water Safety Act in a way that creates an especially hazardous condition, what may the officer do?
choice_a: Nothing; officers may only issue a citation after the voyage is complete
choice_b: Immediately impound and sell the vessel
choice_c: Direct the operator to return to mooring, after which the vessel may not be used again until the condition is corrected
choice_d: Order the vessel to continue on but only at reduced speed
explanation: Section 31.124(f) allows an officer who finds an especially hazardous condition to direct the operator to return to mooring, after which the vessel may not be used until the condition creating the violation is corrected.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.124(f) -- officer authority over hazardous vessels

question: What conduct does Parks and Wildlife Code Section 31.094 (Reckless or Negligent Operation) prohibit?
choice_a: Any operation of a vessel faster than 5 miles per hour
choice_b: Only operating a vessel while towing water skis
choice_c: Texas law has no separate offense for negligent operation, only for BWI
choice_d: Operating a motorboat or vessel in a wilfully or wantonly reckless or negligent manner that endangers the life, limb, or property of any person
explanation: Section 31.094 prohibits operating a motorboat or vessel (or manipulating water skis, an aquaplane, or similar device) in a wilfully or wantonly reckless or negligent manner that endangers the life, limb, or property of any person.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.094 -- reckless or negligent operation

question: When an enforcement officer arrests someone for a Water Safety Act violation, what alternative to an immediate court appearance may the officer use?
choice_a: Deliver a written notice to appear within 15 days before the justice court with jurisdiction, which the person signs promising to appear
choice_b: The officer has no discretion and must always take the person into custody immediately
choice_c: The person must pay the maximum fine on the spot in cash
choice_d: The vessel is automatically forfeited in lieu of any court appearance
explanation: Section 31.125(a) allows an enforcement officer who arrests a person for a Chapter 31 violation to deliver a written notice to appear within 15 days before the justice court having jurisdiction, in lieu of an immediate appearance.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.125(a) -- notice to appear

question: What happens if a person who signed a notice to appear for a Water Safety Act violation fails to appear before the court as promised?
choice_a: There is no consequence for missing the court date
choice_b: Failure to appear is itself a violation of the chapter, and a warrant for the person's arrest may be issued
choice_c: The original citation is automatically dismissed
choice_d: The person's boat registration is instantly and permanently revoked, with no other remedy available
explanation: Section 31.125(b) provides that failing to appear before the court having jurisdiction is itself a violation of the chapter, and a warrant may be issued for the person's arrest.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.125(b) -- consequence of failing to appear

question: What is the general default penalty classification for a Water Safety Act violation that Parks and Wildlife Code Chapter 31 does not otherwise specifically classify?
choice_b: There is no default; unclassified violations cannot be prosecuted
choice_c: A Class C Parks and Wildlife Code misdemeanor
explanation: Section 31.127(a) sets the default penalty for a Chapter 31 violation not otherwise specifically classified as a Class C Parks and Wildlife Code misdemeanor.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.127(a) -- default misdemeanor classification

question: Are written boating incident reports filed with TPWD freely available to any member of the public simply upon request?
choice_a: Yes, anyone may obtain a full, unredacted copy simply by asking
choice_b: No, incident reports are destroyed immediately after filing and cannot be released to anyone
choice_c: Only the vessel's manufacturer may ever see an incident report
choice_d: No -- incident reports are confidential and are released only to specified parties, such as the department, authorized government officials, courts acting under subpoena, and directly concerned persons like the parties involved or their insurers
explanation: Section 31.1055(c)-(d) makes incident reports confidential, releasable only to the department, authorized federal/state/local officials, courts with pending cases under subpoena, and directly concerned persons such as involved parties, owners, or insurance carriers.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.1055(c)-(d) -- confidentiality of incident reports

question: When TPWD releases a boating incident report to a licensed media outlet, what information must it withhold?
choice_a: Personal identifying information, street addresses (other than zip code), telephone numbers, and officer badge numbers, among other protected details
choice_b: Nothing; media outlets receive the complete, unredacted report
choice_c: Only the date of the incident
choice_d: The general location of the incident, which is always withheld from everyone
explanation: Section 31.1055(f) requires TPWD to withhold personal identifying information, addresses other than zip codes, phone numbers, vessel registration/hull numbers, officer badge numbers, and certain other details when releasing a report to media.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.1055(f) -- required redactions for media release

question: Even though individual incident reports are confidential, what public information is TPWD required to compile and publish under Section 31.1055?
choice_a: The full name and home address of every boater involved in any incident that year
choice_b: Annual statistics on the number, causes, and locations of boating incidents
choice_c: TPWD is not required to publish any incident-related statistics
choice_d: A list of every game warden's individual arrest record
explanation: Section 31.1055(e) requires TPWD to publish annual statistics on the number, causes, and locations of boating incidents, even though the underlying individual reports remain confidential.
source_note: Texas Parks & Wildlife Code Section 31.1055(e) -- annual incident statistics
